 Historic flooding in South Florida closes schools, leaves residents stranded in deluge 
 Find live updates of the latest breaking news across South Florida. 
 By Briana Trujillo , Adam Berg and NBC6 • 
 Published November 18, 2026 • 
 Updated 6 minutes ago 
 BOOKMARKER 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 A slow-moving storm system dumped heavy rains in South Florida, flooding some streets and homes, closing sections of highways and collapsing the roof of a synagogue Wednesday. NBC6 has team coverage
 What to Know
 A flood watch remains in effect on Wednesday for much of South Florida after storms dumped several inches of rain over the region—more than a foot in some spots—on Tuesday and Tuesday night along with hail up to one inch, about the size of a quarter. 
 Broward County Public Schools are closed and will remain closed Thursday. Broward County declared a local state of emergency. 
 Miami-Dade County Public Schools will also close Thursday, NBC6 confirmed.
 Several cities in South Florida are feeling the impacts. Fort Lauderdale and Hollywood have issued their own emergency alerts. Miami Beach and Hollywood are waiving fees at city-owned parking garages for residents. 
 A temporary ground stop has been lifted at Miami International Airport (MIA) and Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (FLL).
 Scattered showers and thunderstorms are still expected for Thursday, but better conditions Friday and sunshine expected for the weekend.
 Live coverage has concluded. Click here for the latest on weather. 
 Families rescued, neighborhoods underwater in Hollywood after historic flooding
 Parts of Broward County were underwater Wednesday, prompting county officials to declare a state of emergency.
 In Hollywood, the water rose so high that some people couldn’t leave their homes without help. Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission officers spent hours rescuing people from their homes.
 Samantha Giron's apartment complex saw some of the worst of the flooding. She says her car is ruined after water filled the inside.
 “All over Broward County (flooding) happens all the time but this has never (happened), I've lived here my whole life,” Giron said. “I'm actually just very emotional because I've had this car since forever and it's my first car so it's very emotional.”
 Several of Giron’s neighbors who live on the first floor are now trying to dry out their apartments after water came rushing in.
 “By 1:00 p.m. we had to start moving everything out of the house,” one woman said. “The cars — we have three cars; two are totaled. One seems to be running because we lifted it up, and inside is everything we could salvage, just the mattresses. The rest of the furniture is ruined.”
 Despite the ruined furniture and cars, Giron like many of her neighbors is thankful.
 “I feel awful because I want to help but what are you going to do, we're all needing help right now,” Giron said. “We are more than grateful that there aren't any injuries reported around here, we've been checking on our neighbors, thankfully everybody is okay,” Giron said.
 Giron is focusing on what she still has.
 “At least it's limited to the car and those are replaceable, what matters is our safety,” Giron said.
 Hollywood’s department directors gave an update Wednesday night. Between fire rescue and police, there were nearly 90 calls for service. The city opened a shelter and have already housed six people. Parking enforcement is suspended and city garages are free parking for residents.
 Stay out of floodwater: Why it's dangerous and what to do if you're exposed
 As South Florida deals with the impacts of historic flooding , you may have seen the viral videos of people kayaking and wakeboarding in the deluge.
 While wading out into a flooded parking lot may sound fun, getting into floodwater and standing water can be dangerous and may make you vulnerable to infectious diseases, chemical hazards and injuries, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention .
 Why is floodwater dangerous?
 Floodwater can contain a range of hidden health and safety hazards, from sewage, chemicals and disease-causing germs to coal ash containing substances such as arsenic, chromium and mercury, the CDC said.
 There can also be dangers that are difficult to see beneath the water, including downed power lines, vehicles and debris. Flooding can also displace rodents, snakes and other animals.
 What can floodwater expose you to?
 Coming into contact with contaminated floodwater can lead to infections, skin rashes, gastrointestinal illness and tetanus. In some cases, it can also expose people to less common diseases, including leptospirosis and melioidosis along the Gulf Coast.
 Health officials say the safest option is to avoid entering floodwater altogether.
 What should I do if I come in contact with floodwater?
 If you come into contact with floodwater, wash your skin with soap and clean water as soon as possible, or use alcohol-based wipes or sanitizer if necessary. Clean any wounds and seek medical attention when needed.
 Contaminated clothing should be washed in hot water with detergent before being worn again. Anyone who must enter floodwater should protect themselves with rubber boots, gloves and goggles.
 NBC6 First Alert forecast – Nov. 18, 2026 evening
 When will the rain stop?
 After historic flooding in South Florida today, things are absolutely beginning to improve, but we’re not completely out of the woods. 
 Some storms, much more scattered in nature, can come through tonight and Thursday, and any downpour could trigger a flood advisory or flash flood warning, but there should be less rain and less flooding. A Flood Watch continues for Dade/Broward through Thursday evening. 
 Beaches will have dangerous rip currents through Friday evening. 
 Friday may actually be a decent beach day, and the weekend looks fantastic. 
 Broward and Miami-Dade courts will be closed tomorrow
 Broward and Miami-Dade courts will remain closed Thursday due to flooding, the 11th Judicial Circuit of Florida announced.
 Those with scheduled hearings or other legal proceedings should stay tuned for instructions regarding rescheduling and any updates from court officials.
